text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

THE TIMES - Tripartite decion-making process to be strengthened, prime minister says. Prime Minister Alfred Sant addressed the annual meeting of the Employers' Association on Tuesday, saying the social partners will be consulted more in decision-making in the same manner as they were consulted on the removal of Value Added Tax.
- Malta and Spain sign cultural agreement.
L-ORIZZONT - Efforts continuing for Malta to be a cruise liner base.
- Gozo Channel line loses thousands of liri. The line links Malta with the sister island of Gozo. Its profits have been hurt by rising costs and competition from a helicopter service.
IN- NAZZJON - Federation of Industry president insists government should negotiate international financial assistance for economic restructuring.

- The EU is considering Malta's proposals. Foreign Minister George Vella told EU foreign ministers on Monday Malta was no longer interested in membership but wanted a new structure of talks to bring the two sides closer.
